podcast.title: Brother-in-Law's Bankrupt Label
podcast.body: Harvey Fuqua's brother-in-law owned a small Detroit label that distributed a handful of records through Chess Records, co-writing several hits for Jackie Wilson, before eventually going bankrupt. "Chess also distributed a handful of records from a small Detroit label owned by Harvey Foucault's brother-in-law, who co-wrote several hits for Jackie Wilson before that label went bankrupt."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Co-founding New Birth
podcast.body: After The Marvelettes split, Harvey Fuqua co-founded the 17-piece funk band New Birth by joining forces with the group Love Peace and Happiness, which included Anne Bogan. "That group then joined with Harvey Fouqua in a 17 piece funk band called New Birth."

podcast.title: Discovery and Duets with Anne Bogan
podcast.body: Harvey Fuqua discovered Anne Bogan, a versatile singer, and recorded several duets with her. He later suggested her as a replacement for Gladys Horton in The Marvelettes. "Harvey Fouque was suggested Anne Bogan, who he'd discovered a while before, and recorded a few duets with."

podcast.title: Transition to Gordy Family Labels
podcast.body: Harvey Fuqua was a member of the final lineup of The Moon Glows before transitioning to work for the Gordy family labels, signaling his move into a more production and talent-spotting role within the Motown ecosystem. "a young man who had been a member of the last lineup of the Moon Glows before Harvey Fouqua had moved over to working for the Gordy family labels"
